issue: The 2021 prose assigns γ-eudesmyl cannabigerolate and α-cadinyl cannabigerolate the already-used numbers 37 and 38.
resolution: Preserve 37=cannabinerolic acid and 38=5-acetyl-4-hydroxy-cannabigerol; map the two CBGA esters to 39 and 40 in figure/order, with γ-eudesmyl first and α-cadinyl second.

issue: The 2021 prose later calls cannabicitran 'CBT, 104', conflicting with its own list/figure.
The review explicitly cautions that the two ethoxy cannabitriols are most likely artifacts because ethanol was used during isolation.
resolution: Keep them in the immutable 125 baseline, but mark natural-occurrence status as artifact-cautioned instead of treating them as unquestioned plant biosynthetic products.

issue: The review reports CBLA formation by natural irradiation of CBCA during storage.
resolution: Keep in baseline and distinguish occurrence/transformation evidence from direct biosynthetic origin.

issue: Radwan-125 retains THCA-B as a historical cannabinoid record, while later biosynthesis review literature notes subsequent studies did not confirm its occurrence.
resolution: Preserve baseline identity/number; lower occurrence confidence and flag as historically catalogued but contested.

issue: Experimental section calls it 6′-hydroxy-Δ7′,8′-dihydrocannabinerol, while the text describes it as a derivative of cannabinerolic acid and the NMR assignment includes a COOH carbon.
resolution: Preserve source-reported name verbatim; flag nomenclature inconsistency; do not silently rename it.

issue: The paper fully characterizes compound 10 but does not assign a trivial name.
resolution: Use permanent Atlas ID plus source-numbered descriptive label; do not invent a name.
